note: From gcd(x,y,z)=1, any prime common to two of x,y,z divides the third via x^2+y^2=z^2, hence the entries are pairwise coprime. Exactly one of x,y is even; interchange to make y even, so x,z odd. Put A=(z+x)/2 and B=(z-x)/2. Then gcd(A,B)=1 and AB=(y/2)^2. Coprime factors of a square are squares by prime-exponent parity, say A=m^2,B=n^2. This yields x=m^2-n^2,y=2mn,z=m^2+n^2; x odd forces m,n opposite parity, and gcd(A,B)=1 forces gcd(m,n)=1. Converse identity is direct; no common prime can divide all three because p=2 misses odd x,z, while odd p dividing x,z divides 2m^2 and 2n^2 and hence m,n.
